body.statement: For every valid finite binary-rational encoding \(\mathfrak E\), the finite monotone primal-dual certificate algorithm using the explicit resolution schedule terminates. It performs at most \(MKN_{\mathrm{prior}}N_{\mathrm{state}}N_{\mathrm{quad}}\) interval transition evaluations at \(p_{\mathrm{cert}}\)-bit fractional precision, followed by a finite linear program with at most \(N_{\mathrm{prior}}\) policy columns and \(M\) scenario rows, and returns \(\underline V_{\varepsilon}\leq V\leq\overline V_{\varepsilon}\) with \(\overline V_{\varepsilon}-\underline V_{\varepsilon}\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\). Its eight-entry ledger separately bounds terminal regularization, score-box exit, Gaussian-tail truncation, Gaussian-cell quadrature, time-score-clock interpolation, prior-net discretization, oracle offsets, and outward rounding by \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}/8\) each. The algorithm returns an attained net prior and a finite mixture of net Bayes policies with maximum diffusion scenario regret at most \(\overline V_{\varepsilon}\); for all sufficiently large \(n\), boundary-stable policy transfer yields a predictable \(\pi_n\) with \(\max_m r_{n,m}(\pi_n)\leq\overline V_{\varepsilon}+o(1)\).
body.justification: The finite input model, resolution schedule, stopping bound, interval precision, and separated errors make the multidimensional certificate independently reproducible from primitive scenario data.
body.gap: Baas, ter Schure, and van Rosmalen provide a scalar finite-horizon recursion, and Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu provide an approximate sparse enrichment program; those works inform the construction but do not certify this continuum minimax value or a response-adaptive policy mixture.
body.consumer: The certificate can be attached to recruitment tables used by rpact and to finite-stage decision rules used by interAdapt.

obligation.what_is_open: A complete boundary extension, interval interpolation rule, Gaussian-cell enclosure, and certified oracle and recovered-policy evaluation must be specified and proved to approximate the controlled Bellman semigroup closely enough to place \(V\) inside the claimed interval with the eight advertised error budgets.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen handle specifies only qualitative order preservation, outward rounding, truncation, and finite grids. Those properties enclose the chosen discrete recursion but do not bound its distance from the continuous value. A concrete admissible underdetermination witness is the outward interval rule that widens every continuation interval to the unit interval: it is monotone, terminating, and enclosing, but has width one for every requested tolerance below one.
obligation.attempted: I extended the prior partial proof by deriving the terminal regularization budget, a uniform controlled-score exit bound without forced exploration, a constructive prior-net packing bound with the advertised cardinality, the prior-discretization error through the least-favorable dual identity, the transition-count and termination bounds, and the one-unit rounding allowance. I also tested whether order preservation plus outward rounding could imply the missing consistency bound; the unit-interval witness shows that it cannot.
obligation.partial_result:
The following components of the proposed certificate are derivable from the frozen core.

First set \(e=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\), \(r=r_\delta\), and
\(a=2^{-r}\).  Validity of \(\mathfrak E\) gives \(0<e<1\),
\(K\geq2\), \(M\geq1\), and \(H>0\).  By the displayed definition of
\(r_\delta\),
\[
 2^r\geq2,\qquad
 2^r\geq\frac{32K}{19e},\qquad
 2^r\geq\frac{2H}{\log 19},\qquad
 2^r\geq
 \frac{8\log(64K/e)}{(\log 19)^2}.
\]
All quantities are positive, so taking reciprocals gives
\[
 a\leq\frac12,qquad
 a\leq\frac{19e}{32K},\qquad
 Ha\leq\frac{\log 19}{2},\qquad
 a\leq\frac{(\log 19)^2}{8\log(64K/e)}.
 \tag{1}
\]
The resolution schedule gives
\(\eta_{\mathrm{cert}}=a\) and
\(\delta_{\mathrm{cert}}=a^2\).  In particular,
\(20-a^2\geq19\).  The inequality \(\log(1+y)\leq y\) for
\(y\geq0\), followed by (1), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{shift}}(a^2,a)}{2}
 &=\frac{1}{2a}
 \log\!\left(1+\frac{2Ka^2}{20-a^2}\right)\\
 &\leq\frac{Ka}{20-a^2}
 \leq\frac{Ka}{19}
 \leq\frac e{32}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{2}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \log(20-a^2)-Ha\geq\frac{\log19}{2}>0,
\]
and hence the last inequality in (1) yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 2K\exp\!\left\{-
 \frac{(\log(20-a^2)-Ha)^2}{2a}\right\}
 &\leq 2K\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(\log19)^2}{8a}\right\}\\
 &\leq 2K\exp\{-\log(64K/e)\}
 =\frac e{32}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{3}
\]
By (2)--(3) and the definition of \(\rho_{H,K}\),
\[
 \rho_{H,K}(\delta_{\mathrm{cert}},\eta_{\mathrm{cert}})
 \leq \frac e{16}.
 \tag{4}
\]
The already proved quantitative terminal-comparison lemma therefore bounds
both the finite and diffusion Bayes-envelope gaps, as well as each
corresponding scenario-oracle gap, by \(e/16\).  If the regularized oracle
values are denoted temporarily by \(c_{m,\delta}^{-}\) and
\(c_{m,\delta}^{+}\), then for every \(\lambda\in\Delta_M\) the part of a
dual upper-minus-lower gap caused by terminal regularization is at most
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &B_\delta^+(\lambda)-B_\delta^-(\lambda)
 +\sum_{m=1}^M\lambda_m
 \left(c_{m,\delta}^+-c_{m,\delta}^-\right)\\
 &\hspace{35mm}\leq\frac e{16}
 +\sum_{m=1}^M\lambda_m\frac e{16}
 =\frac e8,
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{5}
\]
using \(\lambda_m\geq0\) and \(\sum_m\lambda_m=1\).  This argument uses no
positive lower bound on any allocation clock.

Second, the displayed score box has a uniform exit bound.  For fixed
\(m\), \(u\in\mathcal U\), and \(j\), write
\[
 M_j(t)=\int_0^t\sqrt{u_j(s)}\,dW_j(s).
\]
The controlled score equation and the simplex constraint on \(u\) give
\[
 X_j(t)=h_j^mQ_j(t)+M_j(t),\qquad
 Q_j(t)=\int_0^t u_j(s)\,ds,qquad 0\leq Q_j(t)\leq1.
 \tag{6}
\]
For \(\theta>0\), successive conditioning for simple predictable controls
shows that
\(\exp\{\theta M_j(t)-\theta^2Q_j(t)/2\}\) is a nonnegative martingale.
Approximation in the stochastic-integral norm and Fatou's lemma give the
corresponding supermartingale inequality for every progressively measurable
\(u\in\mathcal U\).  Stop this process when \(M_j\) first reaches
\(b>0\), approximate the bounded stopping time by finite-valued stopping
times, and then put \(\theta=b\).  Repeating the argument for \(-M_j\)
gives
\[
 \Pr_m^u\{\sup_{t\leq1}|M_j(t)|\geq b\}
 \leq2e^{-b^2/2}.
 \tag{7}
\]
Since \(|h_j^m|\leq H\), (6) implies
\(\sup_t|h_j^mQ_j(t)|\leq H\).  With
\[
 b=R_{\mathrm{cert}}-H
 =\sqrt{2\log(128K/e)},
\]
equation (7) and a union bound over \(j\in\mathcal J\) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sup_m\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}
 \Pr_m^u\!\left\{\max_j\sup_{t\leq1}|X_j(t)|
 >R_{\mathrm{cert}}\right\}
 &\leq2K\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(R_{\mathrm{cert}}-H)^2}{2}\right\}\\
 &=\frac e{64}\leq\frac e{32}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{8}
\]
Every terminal loss and terminal envelope is in \([0,1]\), so changing it
only on this exit event changes its expectation by no more than the bound in
(8).

Third, the prior-net claim, including its displayed cardinality, is
constructive.  Set
\(r_\lambda=r_{\lambda,\mathrm{cert}}=e/32<1\).  If \(M=1\), the singleton
simplex is its own net.  If \(M\geq2\), let \(d=M-1\), start with all
vertices of \(\Delta_M\), and extend to a maximal set
\(\Lambda_{\mathrm{net}}\) whose distinct points have \(\ell_1\)-distance
strictly greater than \(r_\lambda\).  Maximality makes this an
\(r_\lambda\)-net.  Put \(\tau=r_\lambda/(r_\lambda+2)\) and define
\[
 T_p=(1-\tau)p+\tau\Delta_M,
 \qquad p\in\Lambda_{\mathrm{net}}.
\]
Each \(T_p\) is contained in \(\Delta_M\).  If \(T_p\) and \(T_q\)
intersect, then for some \(v,w\in\Delta_M\),
\((1-\tau)(p-q)=\tau(w-v)\), so
\[
 \|p-q\|_1\leq\frac{2\tau}{1-\tau}=r_\lambda,
\]
contradicting separation.  The homothetic simplexes thus have disjoint
relative interiors, while each has \(d\)-volume \(\tau^d\) times the volume
of \(\Delta_M\).  Consequently
\[
 |\Lambda_{\mathrm{net}}|
 \leq\left(1+\frac2{r_\lambda}\right)^{M-1}
 \leq
 \left(\left\lceil\frac2{r_{\lambda,\mathrm{cert}}}\right\rceil+1\right)^{M-1}
 =N_{\mathrm{prior}}.
 \tag{9}
\]
This net is computable from rational input.  Given finitely many rational
centers, existence of another simplex point at distance greater than
\(r_\lambda\) from every center reduces, after enumerating the coordinate
signs in each \(\ell_1\) distance, to finitely many rational linear
feasibility problems.  Exact rational linear programming either returns a
rational new center or certifies that none exists.  Bound (9) forces
termination, and the initial vertices make the point-mass oracle recursions
reusable.

Define within this derivation
\[
 G(\lambda)=B(\lambda)-\sum_{m=1}^M\lambda_mc_m.
\]
The minimax-regret definitions give
\[
 G(\lambda)=\inf_{u\in\mathcal U}
 \sum_{m=1}^M\lambda_m\{L(u,m)-c_m\}.
 \tag{10}
\]
Because \(0\leq\ell_m\leq1\), one has
\(0\leq c_m\leq L(u,m)\leq1\).  Therefore
\[
 |G(\lambda)-G(\lambda')|
 \leq\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}
 \left|\sum_{m=1}^M(\lambda_m-\lambda'_m)
 \{L(u,m)-c_m\}\right|
 \leq\|\lambda-\lambda'\|_1.
 \tag{11}
\]
The already proved least-favorable-saddle theorem gives
\(V=\max_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}G(\lambda)\).  Combining this identity with
(9)--(11) proves the computable dual discretization bound
\[
 0\leq V-max_{\bar\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathrm{net}}}G(\bar\lambda)
 \leq r_{\lambda,\mathrm{cert}}=\frac e{32}.
 \tag{12}
\]

Finally, every displayed mesh width is positive and finite, so the state,
quadrature, and prior grids are finite.  Reusing the point-mass vertices,
the listed loops have at most
\[
 MKN_{\mathrm{prior}}N_{\mathrm{state}}N_{\mathrm{quad}}
 \tag{13}
\]
scenario-prior-state-control-cell interval-transition evaluations.  The
resulting scenario-risk linear program has at most
\(N_{\mathrm{prior}}\) policy columns and \(M\) rows, so both the loops and
the finite rational linear program terminate.  From the definition of
\(p_{\mathrm{cert}}\),
\[
 2^{-p_{\mathrm{cert}}}
 \leq
 \frac{e}{512MKN_{\mathrm{state}}N_{\mathrm{quad}}N_{\mathrm{prior}}},
\]
and hence the allowance obtained by charging one binary rounding unit to
each listed evaluation is at most \(e/512\).

These computations do not control the remaining ledger entries.  The frozen
handle supplies neither a boundary-extension formula nor a local consistency
inequality for its interval interpolation, Gaussian-cell quadrature,
oracle evaluation, or recovered-policy evaluation.  This is a genuine
logical obstruction, not merely a missing constant: after each named
interpolation, an outward interval implementation may widen the continuation
interval to \([0,1]\).  It remains order preserving, uses
\(p_{\mathrm{cert}}\)-bit endpoints, encloses every bounded continuation
value, and terminates, but its width is one, greater than
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\).  Thus monotonicity, finiteness, and the
proved bounds (4), (8), (12), and (13) cannot establish
\(\underline V_{\varepsilon}\leq V\leq\overline V_{\varepsilon}\), the
advertised total width, or the recovered-policy guarantee without a complete
transition construction and new consistency estimates.
